newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Officials removed at Nigeria's Warri refinery.
newsitem.headline: Officials removed at Nigeria's Warri refinery.

text.p: All top officials of Nigeria's state-run Petroleum Products Marketing Company at Warri oil refinery have been removed, the oil minister said on Sunday.
Dan Etete said the removal followed persistent complaints of delays in loading vessels at Warri which meant that the government had to pay compensation to ship owners.
"Sometimes vessels are said to be delayed at the terminals for about 30 days (and) this has discouraged many vessels from loading at Warri," Etete said.
Warri refinery has a theoretical capacity of 125,000 barrels per day, but has rarely attained that amount.
However, performance has improved since June after the repair of the troubled FCC (Fluid Catalytic Cracking Unit).
"The problem we have now is that of having surplus products awaiting evacuation," refinery manager Edward Denner said during the minister's visit.
